target.title: fix(infra): bound response body read in non-streaming fallback paths
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`readResponseBodySnippet` in `src/infra/http-error-body.ts` has a non-streaming fallback path that calls `response.text()` without any size limit, potentially buffering an entire provider error response into memory before the `maxBytes` check runs. Similarly, `readResponsePrefix` in `src/infra/http-body.ts` has a no-reader fallback that calls `response.arrayBuffer()` without bounds.

This can exhaust Gateway memory when a provider returns an oversized error body.

Fixes #101269

## Why This Change Was Made

1. **Export `readResponsePrefix`** and reuse it in `readResponseBodySnippet` instead of the unbounded `response.text()` path
2. **Add Content-Length guard to `readResponsePrefix`** — when no ReadableStream reader is available, check `Content-Length` header before calling `arrayBuffer()` to avoid materializing oversized bodies
3. **Add null body early return** — when `body` is null, return immediately without calling `arrayBuffer()`
4. **Add tests** for Content-Length gating and null body handling

## User Impact

Gateway error-path memory usage is now bounded at `maxBytes` regardless of whether the response body is a ReadableStream or a plain object. No API or behavior change for callers.

## Evidence

- 24/24 unit tests pass (11 http-error-body + 13 http-body)
- Format and lint pass (`oxfmt`, `oxlint`)
- Real behavior proof passes on CI
- Based on PR #101270 by @Pandah97, with added lint fixes (`Number.parseInt`/`Number.isNaN`)
